name: The Blood Oath and Golconda (Dark Ages)

pages.name: The Blood Oath and Golconda (Dark Ages)

text.content:
Cainite feudalism in the Dark Medieval leans heavily on the blood oath — a bond formed by drinking a vampire's vitae across three separate nights, at least one night apart. The bond is not dependent on the regnant's generation: even a 12th-generation neonate's blood can bind an elder. A Cainite may be fully oathbound to only one regnant at a time, but may hold several thralls or lesser (one- or two-drink) bonds of her own.

The Three Drinks

  • First Drink: The drinker feels drawn to the vampire and experiences strong flashes of emotion, perhaps daydreaming about her or subconsciously seeking her out. No mechanical effect yet, though it should be roleplayed.
  • Second Drink: The drinker now sees the vampire as a central figure in her existence and actively seeks contact with her. She finds it difficult to act directly against the vampire (must win or tie a Simple Test to take a directly harmful action) and is one Trait down resisting the vampire's Social Challenges.
  • Third Drink: The oath is complete. The thrall's earlier passion fades into deep loyalty and belonging; all others become secondary to her regnant. An oathbound thrall can be influenced by her regnant's Dominate without eye contact or even without hearing her voice, and is two Traits down resisting such Social Challenges (generation limits on Dominate still apply).

Resisting and Breaking the Oath

A thrall may resist the bond for a whole scene by spending one Willpower Trait for an indirect action, or one Willpower Trait per turn to physically attack her regnant. The oath fades naturally only through prolonged separation and considerable will: for every month (equal to 12 minus the thrall's permanent Willpower Traits) that she abstains from all contact with her regnant, the binding weakens by one level; Storyteller discretion may shorten this if the regnant grossly mistreated the thrall. The character must roleplay this painful separation and spend Willpower Traits fighting the addiction throughout.

The oath also ends if the regnant dies (the thrall's reaction to that release — elation or psychosomatic pain — is entirely up to the Storyteller); the regnant feels nothing if the thrall dies instead. At the Storyteller's discretion, the Merit: The Love of a character other than the regnant may allow the bond to be broken through extensive roleplay and Storyteller approval.

Golconda and the Bitter Journey

Cainite mythology speaks of Golconda, a legendary state of transcendence and mastery over the Beast; many vampires on the Road of Heaven seek it through the loose process called the Bitter Journey, though few (if any) are ever confirmed to attain it, and the rise of devout Christian, Muslim, and Jewish vampires increasingly condemns the pursuit as a pagan practice. There are no fixed systems for Golconda — each Cainite must find her own path, and Storytellers are encouraged to be extremely demanding. A Cainite must maintain a Road rating and a Conscience rating of at least four Traits to remain on the path; falling below either generally causes any mentors on the path to withdraw until she atones. Possible rewards for demonstrated excellence in roleplaying toward Golconda include:

  • Acceptance: The character accepts her nature fully, without either self-loathing or envy of mortal life.
  • Calm: Immunity to frenzy and Rötschreck, including Discipline powers that cause them.
  • Hunger: Feeding requirements drop drastically — as little as one Blood Trait per week rather than per day.
  • Strength: Generational limits on learning Disciplines no longer apply (other generational limits remain unaffected).
  • Mortality: The rarest and most seductive rumor — that a vampire who reaches true enlightenment might throw off Caine's curse and return to mortal life, typically tied to legends of self-sacrifice, true love, and devotion. Even believers in Golconda usually regard these tales as fanciful; the truth is solely the Storyteller's call.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter Five: Rules, Systems and Drama
